headline: Computational models infer gene regulation and 3D chromatin from single-cell data
label: Single Cell Regulatory Omics Modeling
summary: Interpretable and multimodal models now link chromatin architecture, splicing, and regulatory networks to single-cell and spatial measurements.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of regulatory structure from heterogeneous genomic measurements using interpretable or generative models. On the chromatin side, HiC-LEGO reconstructs 3D genome structures from Hi-C contact maps while preserving TADs and enhancer-promoter proximity, and single-cell HiRES profiling shows that CTCF depletion makes TAD-like boundaries more variable, with SALTAFinder identifying long-range active chromatin clusters. On the transcriptional side, scstruc learns Bayesian network regulatory structures from scRNA-seq, CASREL uses SHAP-based ensembles to link RNA-binding proteins to cell type-specific splicing, and DeepCNet predicts promoter-enhancer interactions from single-cell multiome data. Joint and multimodal approaches include q-intNMF for paired expression and accessibility, WGCNA+ for multi-omics co-expression, SCG for spatially resolved co-expression, and GenoME for multimodal profile generation from DNA sequence. What is new is the attention to single-cell resolution of chromatin domains and regulatory links, alongside interpretable motif, Bayesian, and SHAP-based models.
